en.text: Weight-loss pens. Have you ever used one, or do you know someone who has? Today, more than half of Brazilians are overweight and have an associated comorbidity, while around 20% are already in the obesity range. These medications, commonly known as weight-loss pens, are intended precisely for these people. Three of these medications are approved in Brazil: liraglutide, sold under the brand name Saxenda; semaglutide, known as Wegovy and Ozempic; and tirzepatide, sold as Mounjaro. When you gain weight, your body does everything it can to maintain the weight you have gained. It does not matter how much you exercise or how little you eat. When you take the medication, you feel less hungry and become full more quickly. The medication is like a kick-start, but the treatment is much more complex than that. The problem is that medication alone is not enough. You need to change your lifestyle as a whole by adjusting your diet and exercising. After all, obesity is a chronic disease, like diabetes or hypertension. Even after losing weight, you will not be cured and may regain weight at any time. The assessment of which medication is most appropriate for your case must be individualized and performed by a physician. These medications are sold only with a prescription to protect your health. Improper use without medical guidance can cause adverse effects. People who seek treatment on their own may experience unpleasant side effects, drug interactions, excessive loss of muscle mass known as sarcopenia, hair loss, brittle nails, malnutrition, and even pancreatic toxicity, in addition to the risk of obtaining counterfeit medications. In other words, in the long term, you may lose weight, but you may also lose your health. These medications can help people who need them, but the goal is not to help you lose a few pounds for aesthetic reasons; the goal is to restore health and quality of life.
